english.title: Fail to deliver to registrar office copy of court order deferring dissolution on voluntary winding up
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having applied to **(..SPECIFY COURT..) under section 201(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986 for an order deferring the dissolution of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), failed, within 7 days after the making of such an order, to deliver to the registrar a copy of the order for registration
english.legislation: Contrary to section 201(4) of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.

english.notes:
(i) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that summary proceedings for any offence under any of Parts I to VII of this Act may (without prejudice to any jurisdiction exercisable apart from this subsection) be taken against a body corporate at any place at which the body has a place of business, and against any other person at any place at which he is for the time being.
(ii) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, an information relating to such an offence which is triable by a magistrates' court in England and Wales may be so tried if it is laid at any time within 3 years after the commission of the offence and within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summary proceedings in Scotland for such an offence shall not be commenced after the expiration of 3 years from the commission of the offence.
(iii) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides Subject to this (and notwithstanding anything in [section 136 of the Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995]), such proceedings may (in Scotland) be commenced at any time within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the Lord Advocate's opinion to justify the proceedings came to his knowledge or, where such evidence was reported to him by the Secretary of State, within 12 months after the date on which it came to the knowledge of the latter; and subsection (3) of that section applies for the purpose of this subsection as it applies for the purpose of that section.
(iv) For purposes of section 431, a certificate of the Director of Public Prosecutions, the Lord Advocate or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) as to the date on which such evidence as is referred to above came to his knowledge is conclusive evidence.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding one-fifth of statutory maximum or on a second or subsequent conviction to a fine not exceeding one-fiftieth of the statutory maximum for each day on which the contravention is continued.
